supersedes: docs/re/findings/winit-state1-audio.json (audio.json's slot-14 hypothesis is REFUTED; see finding `slot-14-pic-scratch-aliasing`)
summary: Comprehensive walk of winit_state1_title_and_credits (winit.ovr 0x9f3..0xdc4) covering audio, visual, and timing. KEY FINDING: `audio_play_sound(0xE)` at file 0xb43 does NOT play SOUND14.SND. The 'sound table slot 14' at DGROUP 0x33EC physically overlaps the PIC-loader scratch buffer that `winit_load_pic_by_index(0x27)` writes to at the very start of state-1. By the time the audio call fires, slot 14's '12-byte descriptor' is actually PIC #0x27's kind=9 record, and the sample-buffer pointer at 0x3579+14*4 points to the decoded PIC image bytes (not a .snd buffer). So `audio_play_sound(0xE)` either plays GARBAGE (PIC bytes as samples) if the rate_or_vol byte happens to be non-zero, or is SILENT if it's zero. Either way, it is NOT SOUND14.SND. This explains the user's by-ear observation that 'SOUND14 is not what I hear during the intro.' The prior pass got the call sites right but mis-mapped N=0xE to SOUND14.SND. The same hazard does NOT apply to slot 13 by static analysis — slot 13 IS preloaded with SOUND13.SND — but the user reports SOUND13 also doesn't sound right, which means slot 13's master.hdr record likely has buf_lo==buf_hi==0 (aliased slot) or buf_hi<0 (skip-load), and at playback the alias_id field redirects to a different slot. This cannot be definitively resolved without dumping the actual master archive contents or breaking in DOSBox-X.
method: PyGhidra decomp of winit state-1, winit_preload_sounds (winit 0x291), winit_load_pic_by_index (winit 0x38a), winit_show_pic_in_window (winit 0x8f7), winit_wait_ticks_or_enter (winit 0x9ae), wroot audio_play_sound (image 0x10AAA), wroot audio_play_by_id (image 0x135FD), wroot audio_engine_play (image 0x11462), wroot file_table_resolver (image 0x10882), wroot huffman_load_and_decompress (image 0x133E9), wroot busy_wait (image 0x12858). Raw byte scan of winit state-1 0x9f3..0xdc4 enumerated every 0xE8 (CALL rel16) and 0xE8 with target 0xC546 = audio_play_sound thunk. Static decoding of state-1 string addresses via the winit DGROUP delta 0x3DB7 (verified: rt addr 0x4ff8 = file 0x1241 = 'SOUND00.SND' template).

execution_walk.description: Every observable event in winit_state1_title_and_credits in execution order. Each entry has file_offset (winit.ovr), event_type, target (function called or address read/written), context_args, and a one-line description.

events.details: PUSH BP; MOV BP,SP; ADD SP,-0x72 — 0x72 bytes of local stack: 14-entry credit-scroll arrays (4 × 14-byte tables: appear_tick, field_b, cap, col, token) + scroll_pos + skip_flag + tmp_y + tmp_i + iVar3 + iStack_6 (file handle).
func_0x0000e2a8() — flushes any keystrokes buffered before state-1 starts (so user's earlier keypresses don't immediately skip the title).

Loads kind=9 record 0x27 from master archive into DGROUP 0x33EC..0x33F7 (12 bytes) via file_table_resolver. Then opens 'SOUND%02d.SND' template patched to '0' '%' — wait, actually this builds the filename in local stack buffer (NOT 0x33EC), opens the file, and calls huffman_load_and_decompress(handle, 0, 0, *0x33F0=pic_offset_lo, *0x33F2=pic_offset_hi, 0xE). The huffman_load writes the decoded buffer pointer to *(0x3579 + 0xE*4) = *(0x35B1). PIC 0x27 is almost certainly CREDITS.PIC (the credit-scroll text glyphs). NOTE: this call mutates DGROUP 0x33EC..0x33F7 AND DGROUP 0x35B1..0x35B4 — both of which alias to 'sound table slot 14'. After this call slot 14 contains PIC 0x27's record (NOT SOUND14.SND's record).

Builds prompt string in 0x35EA, then crt_open via thunk 0xf924 → handle in iStack_6. If -1, abort(9). Then func_0x0000f100(handle, 0, 0, 0x51aa, 0, 0) — video-driver call into *(0x1bae). The 0x51aa address resolves to file 0x13f3 = 'T16' (the bytes 'T16' is the suffix; in context this is likely a 4KB buffer or scratch). Then crt_dos_close. This opens CREDITS.PIC again and reads bytes via the video driver — probably loads the font glyphs into 0x51aa (a scratch buffer).

Reads *(uint*)0x4FC6 (video_mode_flags). Per startup-sequence.json, bit 0=EGA, bit 1=CGA, bit 2=T16, bit 3=Hercules. Branches to winit_show_pic_in_window(filename) for the matching mode, OR to abort_with_code(0xc) if no bits set. Filenames (resolved via winit DGROUP delta 0x3DB7): EGA→0x5146='TITLEPAG.EGA', CGA→0x5153='TITLEPAG.CGA', T16→0x5160='TITLEPAG.CGA' (T16 reuses CGA art), Hercules→0x516d='TITLEPAG.T16' (Hercules reuses T16 art).
events.side_effects: winit_show_pic_in_window(filename) creates a 40x25 window at (0,0), stores handle in *0x4FBE (win_handle_titlescreen). Calls audio_wait_for_idle (f0dc → wroot 0x3640). Opens the file, calls f130 (video-driver PIC-decode), f118 (video-driver pre-frame), closes file, calls f13c (video-driver refresh) — title page is now visible on screen.

events.screen_state: Title page (Sir-Tech logo + Wizardry wordmark + dragon art) is fully visible.

events.details: if (skip_flag == 0) wait for 2 × 10 = 20 delay-units OR until ENTER pressed. Wall-clock: 20 calls to busy-wait primitive (wroot 0x12858) which reads *(CS:0x1FE2) inner-count + *(CS:0x1FE4) outer-count. Calibrated on 486DX/33 to ~1 delay-unit ≈ 16-50 ms (uncertain — see TIMING section). Approx wall time: 0.3-1.0 sec.
events.skip_behavior: ENTER aborts wait immediately; sets skip_flag=1 which gates all subsequent wait calls.

events.expected_file_if_no_aliasing: SOUND13.SND (slot 13 IS preloaded by winit_preload_sounds at loop i=13)
events.user_observation_says: User by-ear reports this is NOT SOUND13.SND — likely SOUND05 or similar.
events.static_analysis_conclusion: By static analysis slot 13 is preloaded with SOUND13.SND (preload loops i=0..13). Without dumping master.hdr's kind=9 record 13 dynamically we cannot verify what buf_lo/buf_hi/alias_id values it has. If record 13 has buf_lo==buf_hi==0 (or buf_hi<0), preload SKIPS the file load, the sample buffer pointer for slot 13 stays uninitialized, and at playback the alias_id field at *0x33A0 is used to redirect to another slot's loaded buffer. User's ear is the spec — therefore slot 13 IS aliased.

events.details: Video driver's 'pre-frame' / 'prepare to draw text into PIC window' call on the title window handle. Doesn't change pixels yet.

Renders text-token 0xD at screen column 0x5B=91, row 0x34=52. Token 0xD's semantic content (probably a MSG.DBS string-ID or font-glyph ID) is uncertain without runtime verification, but is consistent with the FIRST LINE of the Bradley credit: 'Fantasy Role-Playing Simulation by'.
Renders text-token 9 at column 0x6B=107, row 0x52=82. Likely the SECOND LINE of the Bradley credit: 'D.W. Bradley' (centered, lower than the first line).
Video driver's refresh-window-from-backbuffer call. The Bradley text becomes visible on screen NOW.

if (skip_flag == 0) wait for 0x48 × 10 = 720 delay-units OR until ENTER. Approx wall time on calibrated CPU: ~10-30 sec (large uncertainty). This is the LONG title-hold — user has time to read the Bradley credit + admire the title art. ENTER bails immediately.
Video driver's window-clear / fill-with-color-0xFFFF (or arg passed-through). Wipes the title window's content (but window stays open).
Screen is now blank inside the title window (Sir-Tech and Bradley credits are gone).

events.expected_file: (does NOT play SOUND14.SND — see slot-14-pic-scratch-aliasing finding)
events.static_analysis_conclusion: Slot 14's 12-byte descriptor at DGROUP 0x33EC was OVERWRITTEN by step 3's winit_load_pic_by_index(0x27) — it now holds PIC 0x27's kind=9 record, not slot 14 of the sound table. The sample buffer pointer at 0x3579+14*4 points to the decoded CREDITS.PIC bytes. audio_play_sound(0xE) reads *0x33F6 (= the rate_or_vol byte of the PIC record). If non-zero, audio_engine_play plays the decoded PIC bytes as audio samples (garbage / brief noise). If zero, audio_engine_play takes its 'stop-current-sound' path (blocks on *0x1764 then returns). Either way it is NOT SOUND14.SND. User's by-ear report of SOUND06 suggests the descriptor's alias_id at *0x33EC happens to point to slot 6 (SOUND06.SND), OR something else routed via PIC record contents. Definitive verification requires DOSBox-X breakpoint + memory dump.

events.details: if (skip_flag == 0) wait 10 × 10 = 100 delay-units OR ENTER. Approx wall time: 1.5-5 sec. Gives the page-clear transition time to register before the next reveal.

events.expected_file: SOUND06.SND (slot 6 preloaded normally — by static analysis)
events.static_analysis_conclusion: Slot 6 is in the i=0..13 preload range; if master.hdr record 6 has valid buf_lo/buf_hi, slot 6 loads SOUND06.SND. User's report that this fires AS the clang lands suggests either (a) slot 6's master.hdr record is aliased to slot 7 (SOUND07.SND), OR (b) the user is conflating this with the next call (audio_play_sound(7) at step 23), OR (c) the timing of the previous N=0xE call is bleeding through. Requires dynamic verification.

events.details: Renders token 7 at col 0x4C=76, row 0x43=67. Token 7 is the STATIC HEADER text — almost certainly 'Wizardry VI' (per prior pass).
Renders token 8 at col 0x4C=76, row 0x63=99. Token 8 is the SECONDARY HEADER text — almost certainly 'Bane of the Cosmic Forge'.
Header text 'Wizardry VI / Bane of the Cosmic Forge' is now on-screen above the (empty) scroll area.

events.expected_file: SOUND07.SND (slot 7 preloaded normally — by static analysis)
events.user_observation_says: User by-ear reports this is the final beat (likely 'clang') aligning with scroll-start.
events.static_analysis_conclusion: By static analysis slot 7 plays SOUND07.SND directly. The user's by-ear mapping is consistent with this if the previous step (audio_play_sound(6)) was actually playing SOUND06 'whoosh' just before. So the user's beat sequence might be: SOUND06=whoosh (call N=6), SOUND07=clang (call N=7). Reconciled this way, only calls N=0xD and N=0xE need alias-explanations.

events.details: if (skip_flag == 0) wait 10 × 10 = 100 delay-units OR ENTER. Gives the user time to register the 'Wizardry VI' header before scroll motion starts.

Initializes 9-entry credit-scroll table on local stack: 4 parallel arrays (cap[9], col[9], appear_tick[9], field_b[9]) plus token[9]. Pre-init values: tokens [7,8,0xC,1,2,3,4,5,6], cols [0x4C,0x4C,8,0x14,0x14,0x14,0x14,0x14,0xE], appear_tick [0,0,0,4,0x24,0x3C,0x58,0x78,0x98], field_b [3,0x23,0xD,0x90,0x90,0x90,0x90,0x90,0x50], cap [3,0x23,0xD,0xD,0xD,0xD,0xD,0xD,0x50]. Entries 0,1,2 are static (appear=0); entries 3..8 scroll in at staggered ticks. Per prior pass.

Main credit-scroll loop. Per frame: f118(-1) clear; for i=8..0: if appear_tick[i] <= scroll_pos compute y; if y >= cap (or i<3 or i==8 clamping rule), render_text_token(token[i], col[i], y); end-for; f13c refresh; mouse_check; if mouse_moved → set skip_flag=0 (continue_flag); kbd_check; if any key → getkey, set skip_flag=0; scroll_pos += 2. Loop exits when scroll_pos > (entry[7].appear + entry[7].field_b - entry[7].cap) = (0x78 + 0x90 - 0xD) = 0xFB = 251 (so ~126 frames at +2/frame), OR when skip_flag is cleared. Each frame includes (1) the clear-frame, (2) up to 9 text-token renders, (3) refresh, (4) input poll. NO per-frame WAIT — frame rate is determined by raw render+poll speed. Per prior pass.
Clear the scroll window.
Re-renders header token 7 at col 76, row 3 (top of window).
Re-renders header token 8 at col 76, row 0x23=35.
Renders token 6 at col 14, row 80. This is the LAST credit-scroll item from the scrolling — fixed at its resting position. Per prior pass, this is likely the 'press any key' or copyright line.
Final post-scroll page is on-screen: Wizardry VI / Bane of the Cosmic Forge / (last item).
Destroys the title window. Subsequent state-2 will recreate it.
Set game_state to 2 — when state-1 returns, wroot's main loop reads game_state and loads winit again (state 2 = init fonts/windows).

if (skip_flag == 0) wait_n_ticks_or_enter(0x1c) — short timed wait (28 delay-units × winit_wait_ticks*10? — actually c43f is the wroot 0x9a3 variant which doesn't *10; total wait is 0x1c=28 ticks ~0.5-2 sec). Else loop polling kbd+mouse until ANY input (indefinite wait). The 'if skip THEN timed wait, else indefinite wait' inversion is intentional: a skipping user already wants to advance; a non-skipping user needs to be given time to read the final post-scroll page. So actually it's INVERSE of what feels intuitive — re-read carefully:  uVar4 starts as 1 if skip_flag==0 (no skip yet); inside the scroll loop uVar4 gets cleared to 0 on mouse/kbd. After the loop, `if (uVar4 == 0)` means skip happened (or pre-scroll skip happened) → timed short wait. `else` (uVar4 == 1) means scroll completed naturally without skip → indefinite wait until user presses any key. This makes UX sense: scroll completed without interruption means user is intentionally watching, so let them stay; scroll was interrupted means user wants to advance, so absorb the input + brief beat to settle.
Final flush of any buffered keystrokes before state 2 runs.

audio_calls_consolidated.user_ear: Likely SOUND05 ('pow') — user reports NOT SOUND13
audio_calls_consolidated.confidence: low — needs DOSBox dump of master.hdr record 13 OR breakpoint dump of slot 13 BSS

audio_calls_consolidated.static_file: DEFINITELY NOT SOUND14.SND (slot 14 = PIC scratch overlap)

audio_calls_consolidated.user_ear: Likely SOUND06 or SOUND07 — user's beat sequence suggests SOUND07

wait_calls_consolidated.context: Between Sirtech splash sound and Bradley credit
Long title-hold; user reads Bradley credit
Between page-clear and Wizardry header reveal
Post-scroll dwell on final page (only if user SKIPPED during scroll); else indefinite wait for any input

findings.claim: DGROUP 0x33EC (= sound-table slot 14's 12-byte descriptor) IS PHYSICALLY THE SAME MEMORY as the PIC-loader scratch buffer. winit_load_pic_by_index() at winit 0x38a unconditionally writes 12 bytes there via file_table_resolver(kind=9, dst=0x33EC, index=pic_idx, mode=0). State-1's very first non-prologue call is winit_load_pic_by_index(0x27), so by the time audio_play_sound(0xE) fires at winit 0xb43, slot 14's descriptor is PIC #0x27's kind=9 record — NOT a valid sound descriptor. Additionally, the huffman_load_and_decompress call inside winit_load_pic_by_index writes the decoded buffer pointer to *(0x3579 + 0xE*4) — overwriting slot 14's sample-buffer pointer with a pointer to the decoded PIC bytes. So audio_play_sound(0xE) reads buf_lo/buf_hi/rate_or_vol/flags from a PIC record AND plays bytes from a decoded PIC image. This was MISSED by docs/re/findings/winit-state1-audio.json, which mapped N=0xE → SOUND14.SND. The 'loop-bound-question' in that finding was the right scent — yes, slot 14 is past the preload bound — but the resolution isn't 'JG vs JGE' or 'separate code path'; it's that slot 14's memory is repurposed by the PIC loader BEFORE the audio call fires.

evidence.details: winit_state1 at 0x9fc: `B8 27 00 50 E8 87 F9` = `MOV AX,0x27; PUSH AX; CALL 0x38a` (= winit_load_pic_by_index(0x27)). winit_load_pic_by_index disasm at 0x03a0..0x03a8: `MOV AX,0x33EC; PUSH AX; MOV AX,0x9; PUSH AX; CALL 0xc31e` — file_table_resolver(kind=9, dst=0x33EC, ...). And at 0x0432..0x0449: builds the huffman call with `MOV AX,0xE; PUSH AX; ...; CALL 0xee85` — last stack arg to huffman_load_and_decompress is 0xE, which is the slot index that gets written to *(0x3579+0xE*4). Cross-check: audio_play_sound at wroot 0x10AAA computes slot 14's descriptor as `*(byte*)(0xE*0xC + 0x334E) = *(byte*)0x33F6` (rate_or_vol field). 0x334E + 0xE*0xC = 0x33F6 ✓. And audio_play_by_id at wroot 0x135FD reads sample-buffer ptr from `*(undefined2 *)(0xE*4 + 0x3579) = *(0x35B1)` and `*(0xE*4 + 0x357B) = *(0x35B3)` — both written by the huffman call inside winit_load_pic_by_index.

findings.implication: audio_play_sound(0xE) at state-1 file 0xb43 either plays GARBAGE (decoded PIC bytes as 8-bit PCM samples — could sound like a click, hiss, or short tone) or is SILENT (if *0x33F6 happens to be zero, audio_engine_play takes the stop-sound path). Neither outcome matches SOUND14.SND. The .snd file SOUND14.SND on disk is loaded somewhere ELSE (maybe never), and the 5506-byte size of SOUND14.SND is incidental.
findings.remediation: The TS port should NOT wire 'scroll-start' transition to SOUND14.SND. Use one of: (a) DOSBox-X breakpoint at audio_play_sound(0xE) to dump the slot-14 memory and identify what's actually playing, (b) consult the user's by-ear observation (SOUND06 reported) and wire to SOUND06.SND, (c) leave it silent and rely on the N=6 and N=7 calls (which are in the preload range) for the scroll-start audible beats.

findings.claim: Five audio_play_sound calls in state-1 (matches prior pass). Byte patterns verified: 0xac2 b8-04, 0xadb b8-0d, 0xb43 b8-0e, 0xb5c b8-06, 0xb90 b8-07. Of these, only N=4 reliably plays its 'named' SOUND04.SND (slot 4 preloaded directly with no aliasing risk). N=0xE is GUARANTEED to NOT play SOUND14.SND (slot-14-pic-scratch-aliasing). N=0xD, 6, 7 might play their 'named' files OR be aliased — depends on master.hdr's kind=9 records 13, 6, 7 (which we don't have static access to).
findings.confidence: high (call sites + N values), medium (file mapping for N=13/6/7 without dynamic verification)

findings.claim: winit_preload_sounds (winit 0x291) called with n_slots=14 (from state-0 at winit 0x873) preloads slots 0..13 inclusive. The exit comparator at 0x37e..0x381 is `CMP AX, [BP+4]; JGE 0x386` — JGE means signed greater-or-equal, so loop body runs while i < n. Slot 14 is NOT preloaded by this call.

evidence.details: 0x37b MOV AX,[BP-0x18]; 0x37e CMP AX,[BP+0x4]; 0x381 JGE 0x386. JGE is signed >=. Loop body at 0x2a2 runs only when i < n_slots. Refutes the 'JG vs JGE' hypothesis in the prior pass.

findings.claim: State-1's vmode dispatch reads *(uint*)0x4FC6 and branches to winit_show_pic_in_window(filename). Filename selection: bit 0 (EGA)→'TITLEPAG.EGA' at winit DGROUP 0x5146, bit 1 (CGA)→'TITLEPAG.CGA' at 0x5153, bit 2 (T16)→'TITLEPAG.CGA' (second copy at 0x5160 — T16 reuses CGA art), bit 3 (Hercules)→'TITLEPAG.T16' at 0x516d (Hercules reuses T16 art). All resolved via winit DGROUP delta 0x3DB7 (verified: file 0x138F = address 0x5146 = 'TITLEPAG.EGA'). Mapping `T16-reuses-CGA, Hercules-reuses-T16` is unintuitive but consistent with engineering history (T16 was probably added later as a CGA variant; Hercules as a T16 variant).

evidence.details: Data strings at file offsets 0x138F='TITLEPAG.EGA', 0x139C='TITLEPAG.CGA', 0x13A9='TITLEPAG.CGA' (duplicate), 0x13B6='TITLEPAG.T16'. State-1 disasm at 0xa20..0xab7 dispatches on bits 0,1,2,3 of *0x4FC6 with the four address-args 0x5146, 0x5153, 0x5160, 0x516D respectively. Resolving via delta 0x3DB7: 0x5146-0x3DB7=0x138F, 0x5153-0x3DB7=0x139C, 0x5160-0x3DB7=0x13A9, 0x516D-0x3DB7=0x13B6 — all matching.

findings.claim: winit_load_pic_by_index(0x27) at state-1 entry loads PIC index 0x27 = 39 from the kind=9 master archive table. This is almost certainly CREDITS.PIC (the credit-scroll text glyphs) — NOT TITLEPAG. Three independent signals support this: (1) right after the load_pic call, state-1 immediately opens 'CREDITS.PIC' BY FILENAME (rt addr 0x513a → file 0x1383 = 'CREDITS.PIC') and reads it via the video driver — this open-by-name plus the load-by-index together suggest CREDITS.PIC is the same file but loaded two ways for different purposes. (2) The vmode-specific TITLEPAG load happens AFTER, in winit_show_pic_in_window(filename) with explicit vmode-suffixed filenames. (3) The credit-scroll loop renders tokens [7,8,0xC,1..6] which would need glyph data — that's what CREDITS.PIC provides.

evidence.details: PIC index 0x27 = file_table_resolver kind=9 idx=39. Filename string 'CREDITS.PIC' lives at file 0x1383 = rt addr 0x513a. State-1 references 0x513a directly with `MOV AX,0x513a` at 0xa0c-0xa0e.

findings.needs: DOSBox-X file-open trace at startup would confirm if CREDITS.PIC is opened twice (once by index lookup → archive seek, once by name → standalone file) or if there are two different files.

findings.claim: winit_load_pic_by_index(0x27) calls huffman_load_and_decompress with slot=0xE (decimal 14) — see disasm at winit 0x0432. This writes the decoded CREDITS.PIC byte segment to *(0x3579 + 14*4) = *(0x35B1) and the offset/length to *(0x357B + 14*4) = *(0x35B3). So slot 14 of the SAMPLE-BUFFER table is bound to the CREDITS.PIC image bytes. This is the second reason why audio_play_sound(0xE) doesn't produce SOUND14.SND: even if slot 14's descriptor weren't corrupt, the sample-buffer pointer ALREADY points to PIC bytes.

evidence.details: Disasm shows `MOV AX,0xE; PUSH AX; PUSH word [0x33F2]; PUSH word [0x33F0]; PUSH 0; PUSH 0; PUSH word [BP-0x22]; CALL 0xee85` — the last (top-of-stack) arg is the slot index 0xE. Cross-check huffman_load_and_decompress decomp: writes `*(in_stack_0000000c + 0x3579) = segment` where in_stack_0000000c = slot*4 = 0xE*4 = 0x38.

findings.claim: If audio_play_sound's computed uVar1 (= rate_or_vol byte at slot+0xA) is zero, audio_engine_play takes its 'stop-current-sound' path: blocks on *0x1764 until non-zero, then calls FUN_1000_1741 (cleanup) and returns without playing anything. This is a silent path — relevant to the slot 14 scenario where the rate_or_vol byte (= PIC record byte at +0xA) happens to be zero, in which case audio_play_sound(0xE) is completely silent.

evidence.details: audio_engine_play decomp lines 39-44: `if (param_6 == '\0') { do {} while (DAT_1000_1764 == '\0'); FUN_1000_1741(); return; }` — where param_6 is the volume arg passed from audio_play_sound. So vol=0 ⇒ stop, no playback.

findings.claim: Per the user-lived-recollection-is-spec auto-memory rule, the user's by-ear observations override static RE for what's actually heard during the intro. The user reports: (1) Sirtech splash = SOUND04 plus possibly others; (2) Title-page reveal (after Bradley credit) = SOUND05+SOUND06+SOUND07 in rapid succession. Mapping calls to user's observations: N=4 → SOUND04 ✓ (matches direct); the three rapid sounds at title-reveal map to N=0xD/0xE/6 or 0xD/6/7. Most parsimonious explanation: N=0xD plays SOUND05 (via aliasing — slot 13's master.hdr record has buf=0 and alias_id=5), N=0xE plays whatever happens to be at the corrupt slot-14 (could be SOUND06 if the post-PIC garbage happens to alias-id=6, or could be intentionally PIC-bytes-as-noise = audible whoosh sound), N=6 plays SOUND06 directly OR is also aliased, N=7 plays SOUND07. This still leaves ambiguity that requires DOSBox-X verification.

evidence.details: User's direct observation in conversation: 'SOUND13 and SOUND14 are NOT what the user hears during the intro' + 'Title-page reveal: three sounds in rapid succession — SOUND05 (pow), SOUND06 (whoosh), SOUND07 (clang).'

findings.confidence: medium (user's ear) / low (specific N→file mapping for aliased slots)

findings.claim: After the scroll loop, state-1 does: `if (skip_happened) timed_wait(0x1c); else indefinite_wait_until_input`. This may seem inverted but is UX-correct: a user who skipped is signaling 'advance now' so a brief wait absorbs final keystrokes; a user who watched naturally is given an indefinite admire-the-final-page pause until they explicitly press a key.

evidence.details: winit_state1 decomp lines 247-261: `if (uVar4 == 0) { c43f(0x1c); } else { do { kbd; mouse; } while (no_input); }`. uVar4 = 0 when skip happened (mouse/kbd hit during scroll loop).

delay_primitive.name: delay_primitive_busy_wait
delay_primitive.behavior: Read calibration constants at boot. Inner loop runs *(0x1FE2) iterations of decrement-and-compare-against-0x206b (typically 0); outer loop runs *(0x1FE4) passes. Wall-time per call is CPU-speed-dependent.
delay_primitive.best_estimate_on_486dx_33: 1 delay-unit ≈ 50ms (so 'wait_n_ticks_or_enter(n)' = n*10 calls ≈ 500ms per n=1, 10s per n=20)
delay_primitive.calibration_quality_note: Per CLAUDE.md 'Wall-clock parity ≠ byte parity' — the original CRT busy-wait calibration writes to *(CS:0x1FE2/0x1FE4) at boot and depends on the actual CPU. DOSBox-X's cycles=fixed doesn't faithfully reproduce this. Aim for byte parity on the math and TUNE per-frame interval to feel right; don't aim for wall-clock parity.
delay_primitive.verification_method: Static analysis only confirms the math: n_arg × 10 = total number of busy-wait calls. Translating to wall-clock requires (a) trusting the CRT calibration, (b) running DOSBox-X with known cycles setting to measure, or (c) tuning to user-perceived feel.

post_scroll_c43f_variant.name: wait_n_ticks_or_enter_no_x10
post_scroll_c43f_variant.claim: The post-scroll wait at winit 0xdee calls c43f (wroot 0x9a3) with arg 0x1c. Per prior pass this is wroot's own wait-or-enter variant; whether it also has the ×10 multiplier requires PyGhidra decomp of wroot 0x9a3. By the symmetry with winit 0x9ae (which does have ×10), wroot 0x9a3 LIKELY also has ×10 — in which case 0x1c × 10 = 280 delay-units (~14 sec). But this is unverified.
post_scroll_c43f_variant.needs: Decomp wroot 0x9a3 to confirm whether it has the ×10 multiplier.

user_visible_sequence: 1. State-1 entry: kbd_flush, load CREDITS.PIC glyphs (PIC #0x27) into slot-14 sample buffer (writes 12 bytes to 0x33EC), open + read CREDITS.PIC again via video driver.
2. Vmode dispatch → winit_show_pic_in_window(TITLEPAG.{EGA|CGA|T16|HRC}) — title window 0x4FBE is created (40×25 fullscreen overlay), title art rendered.
3. AUDIO_CALL_1: audio_play_sound(4) → SOUND04.SND (Sirtech splash sound, e.g. door click).
4. WAIT: 2×10=20 delay-units (~1s) or ENTER.
5. AUDIO_CALL_2: audio_play_sound(0xD) → user-by-ear: SOUND05 (pow). Static analysis says SOUND13.SND if not aliased; user evidence implies aliased.
6. Pre-frame video setup, render text-token 0xD at (col 91, row 52), render text-token 9 at (col 107, row 82), refresh — Bradley credit visible.
7. WAIT: 0x48×10=720 delay-units (~10-30s) or ENTER. LONG title-hold.
8. f118 clear + f13c refresh — title window goes blank.
9. AUDIO_CALL_3: audio_play_sound(0xE) → user-by-ear: SOUND06 (whoosh). Static analysis: NOT SOUND14 (slot 14 is PIC-scratch overlap).
10. WAIT: 10×10=100 delay-units (~3s) or ENTER.
11. AUDIO_CALL_4: audio_play_sound(6) → user-by-ear: part of title-reveal beat. Static analysis: SOUND06.SND if not aliased.
12. Render token 7 at (76, 67) and token 8 at (76, 99) — 'Wizardry VI' + 'Bane of the Cosmic Forge' static header. Refresh.
13. AUDIO_CALL_5: audio_play_sound(7) → user-by-ear: final beat (clang). Static analysis: SOUND07.SND if not aliased.
14. WAIT: 10×10=100 delay-units (~3s) or ENTER.
15. Credit-scroll table init (9 entries, tokens [7,8,0xC,1,2,3,4,5,6] with their cols/rows/appear-ticks).
16. Scroll loop ~126 frames at scroll_pos += 2/frame. Per frame: clear, render visible entries with clamping, refresh, poll mouse+kbd. Skip on any input.
17. Post-scroll: clear, render tokens 7 + 8 + 6 at fixed positions for 'final state' page. Refresh.
18. Destroy title window 0x4FBE. Set *0x363a := 2 (advance to state 2).
19. Post-state-wait: if user skipped → c43f(0x1c) brief absorb-input wait; else loop polling kbd+mouse indefinitely until any input.
20. kbd_flush_buffer. Return — wroot reloads winit for state 2.

next_steps_for_user: 1. Run DOSBox-X with breakpoints at wroot file_offset 0xAAA (= image 0x10AAA = audio_play_sound entry). At each break, dump BX register and memory at DGROUP 0x33EC..0x33F7 (for slot 14 access) or 0x33A0..0x33AB (slot 13), plus 0x35AD..0x35B5 (sample-buffer ptrs slots 11-14). This will definitively settle which file plays for each N value in state-1.

2. Alternatively: use the DOSBox-X file-open logging (tools/dosbox/run-with-logging.sh) to count how many SOUND<NN>.SND files are opened during state-0 + state-1. If only 8-10 are opened (instead of all 12 present 00-13 files), the missing slots are aliases.
3. Once verified, update docs/re/findings/winit-state1-audio.json's alias-table OR replace it with this finding's data. Promote the corrected SOUND-file mapping to docs/re/snd-format.md.

scripts_used: /tmp/dump_state1_deepdive.py — decompile + raw disasm of all relevant functions
operational_notes.key_quirk_1: winit.ovr's data section is reached via DGROUP delta 0x3DB7: rt_addr − 0x3DB7 = file_offset. Verified rt addr 0x4FF8 = file 0x1241 = 'SOUND00.SND' template, rt addr 0x5146 = file 0x138F = 'TITLEPAG.EGA'.
operational_notes.key_quirk_2: kind=9 records in the master archive are 12 bytes each. PIC indices and SOUND indices share the SAME table; sound preload uses indices 0..13, PIC loads use indices 0x22 (graveyard) and 0x27 (credits/title — likely CREDITS.PIC). The 'slot 14' of the audio sound-table at DGROUP 0x33EC physically overlaps the PIC scratch buffer — there is no real slot 14 of the sound table.
operational_notes.key_quirk_3: audio_play_sound's slot-14 access reads bytes that were written by the most-recent winit_load_pic_by_index call. State-1's startup sequence makes this DETERMINISTIC: PIC 0x27 is loaded immediately on state-1 entry, so by the time audio_play_sound(0xE) fires, the bytes at 0x33EC are PIC #0x27's record contents. Treating them as a sound descriptor produces undefined audio behavior.
